t.1.56.1: Then, his heart burning with anguish as he remembered his own defeat, sighing again and again, he who had made an enemy of the great-souled one…
t.1.56.2: Having gone to the southern region together with his queen, O Rāghava, Viśvāmitra of great austerities performed a supreme and terrible penance. Living on fruits and roots and self-restrained, he practised the highest austerity.
t.1.56.3: Then sons were born to him, devoted to truth and righteousness: Haviṣyanda, Madhuṣyanda, Dṛḍhanetra and Mahāratha.
t.1.56.4: When a thousand years were complete, Brahmā, the grandsire of the worlds, spoke sweet words to Viśvāmitra, whose wealth was his austerity.
t.1.56.5: O son of Kuśika, by your austerity you have won the worlds of the royal sages; by this austerity indeed we know you to be a royal sage.
t.1.56.6: Having spoken thus, the greatly radiant supreme lord of the worlds went, together with the gods, to heaven, to Brahmaloka.
t.1.56.8: I have performed very great austerity, and all the gods together with the hosts of sages know me as a royal sage; yet I think there is no fruit of austerity.
t.1.56.7: Viśvāmitra too, having heard that, his face somewhat downcast with shame, overcome by great sorrow and filled with anger, spoke these words.
t.1.56.9: Having thus resolved in his mind, O Kākutstha, the great ascetic, supremely self-controlled, once again practised the most intense austerity.
t.1.56.10: At that very time there was a delight of the Ikṣvāku race, renowned as Triśaṅku, truthful in speech and master of his senses.
t.1.56.11: O Rāghava, this resolve arose in him: "May I perform a sacrifice, and may I go in my own body to the supreme abode of the gods."
t.1.56.13: Rejected by Vasiṣṭha, he went to the southern direction, where the Vasiṣṭhas, rich in long austerity, had performed their penance.
t.1.56.12: He summoned Vasiṣṭha and told him what he had in mind, and he was told by the great-souled Vasiṣṭha, "It is impossible."
t.1.56.14: Triśaṅku, of exceedingly great splendour, beheld the hundred sons of Vasiṣṭha, supremely radiant and illustrious, engaged in austerities.
t.1.56.15: Approaching all the great-souled sons of his guru and saluting them one after another in due order, he of very great splendor, his face bowed a little in shame, addressed them all with joined palms.
t.1.56.16: I take refuge in you, who are worthy of giving refuge; I have come to you seeking shelter. I have been rejected by the great-souled Vasiṣṭha; may good fortune be yours.
t.1.56.17: Desiring to perform a great sacrifice, I ask that you permit it. Bowing to all of you, the sons of my preceptor, I seek your favour.
t.1.56.18: Bowing low with my head, I entreat the brāhmaṇas established in austerity: may you, sirs, with focused minds, perform a sacrifice for me to bring about my success, so that I may attain the world of the gods in this very body.
t.1.56.19: Rejected by Vasiṣṭha, O ascetics rich in penance, I see no other refuge at all except all of you, the sons of my guru.
t.1.56.20: For the family priest is the supreme refuge of all the Ikṣvākus; and next after him, all of you are my deity.
